About this program
Forest Science, Doctor of Philosophy
Advance scientific understanding and develop solutions to complex challenges facing forests and natural resources through innovative research while preparing for leadership in research, teaching, and the future of forest science.
Advance Forest Science
Prepare to become a research leader, scientist, or educator addressing the complex challenges facing forests and natural resources. Working closely with faculty mentors, you'll develop expertise in a specialized area of forest science while conducting original research that advances scientific understanding and informs forest management and policy.
You'll build advanced skills in research methods, quantitative analysis, scientific communication, and college teaching while pursuing one of three concentrations: ecosystem science, forest management sciences, or forest social sciences. Through independent scholarship and interdisciplinary collaboration, you'll contribute new knowledge that supports the stewardship and sustainable management of forests and natural resources while preparing for careers in academia, government agencies, research institutions, and nonprofit organizations.
Customize your doctoral experience by choosing a concentration that aligns with your research interests and career goals. Whether you're advancing ecological research, developing innovative forest management strategies, or exploring the human dimensions of forestry, you'll pursue specialized study while contributing original research. You'll also choose either additional Forest Science coursework or the interdisciplinary Ecology, Evolution, and Conservation Biology (EECB) emphasis to further tailor your doctoral training.
Ecosystem Science - investigate the ecological processes that shape forest ecosystems and support their long-term health and resilience.
Forest Management Sciences - explore science-based approaches to sustainable forest management, restoration, and natural resource stewardship.
Forest Social Sciences - examine how people, policy, economics, and communities influence forest management and natural resource decisions.
A community of discovery
Pursue your doctoral research in one of the nation's premier environments for forest science. Surrounded by diverse forest ecosystems, public lands, and active forest management and restoration projects, you'll investigate real-world challenges while contributing research that informs the future of forest stewardship. Working closely with faculty mentors, you'll design an individualized program of study that reflects your research interests and long-term goals. Through collaborations with partners including the Ecological Restoration Institute, the U.S. Forest Service, and other research organizations, you'll engage with complex forestry challenges while building a strong foundation for a career in research, higher education, or natural resource leadership. Students interested in ecology and conservation can also pursue an optional emphasis in Ecology, Evolution, and Conservation Biology (EECB).
Shaping the future of forestry
Lead the future of forest science through careers in research, higher education, and natural resource leadership. Graduates pursue careers as university faculty, research scientists, and leaders in government agencies, nonprofit organizations, consulting firms, and private industry. Whether you're advancing scientific knowledge, informing forest management and policy, or mentoring the next generation of forestry professionals, you'll be prepared to make a lasting impact on the stewardship of forests and natural resources.
Pursue bigger questions
How can forests become more resilient to wildfire and climate change? What management strategies support healthy ecosystems? How do policy, economics, and human values shape the future of forests? As a doctoral student, you'll pursue questions like these while conducting original research that advances forest science and informs natural resource stewardship. Research opportunities span ecosystem processes, forest management, restoration, wildfire, conservation, hydrology, wildlife ecology, forest policy, and the human dimensions of forestry. Whether you're working in the field, analyzing data, or collaborating with faculty and research partners, you'll contribute new knowledge that informs science, management, and policy while helping shape the future of forests and the communities that depend on them.
Graduate contact
Questions about admissions, research opportunities, or faculty expertise? Contact the School of Forestry Graduate Coordinator at ForestryGraduateStudies@nau.edu to learn more about the Forest Science PhD and identify potential faculty mentors.
